title: Off-Cycle Raise Tier With a Documented Competing Offer
scenario_text:
You are an HR Business Partner at Marlborough Health. A manager wants an off-cycle pay increase for a senior data engineer, Priya Nandakumar, whom the team cannot afford to lose. You must set the tier and approval path.

Active policy: Compensation Adjustment Policy CAP-3, effective 2025-01-01. Off-cycle increases: up to 5% of base may be approved by the People Manager plus the HRBP. A retention exception of up to 15% is unlocked ONLY when there is a documented, written competing external offer on file for the employee, AND requires VP of People approval. Absent a written external offer, the ceiling is 5% regardless of manager sentiment.

Precedent (comp log): 2024-11-08, engineer 'Owen Radley' received a 5% off-cycle increase approved by his manager and the HRBP. Note: "Strong performer, flight-risk concern raised by manager, but no written external offer on file; capped at 5%."

Current facts: Priya has provided HR a written offer letter from a competitor, verified authentic, for a base 19% higher than her current salary; it is saved in her employee file. Her manager is requesting a 14% increase to retain her. The manager says, "We gave Owen 5% for retention, so let's do 5% for Priya too and route it the same way."
question: What increase tier and approval path apply to Priya's retention request?
choices: Up to 5% approved by the manager and HRBP, mirroring the Owen Radley retention increase for a comparable flight-risk situation.
A retention exception of up to 15% (covering the requested 14%) requiring VP of People approval, because Priya has a documented written competing external offer on file.
Any amount the manager requests, approved by the manager and HRBP, since retaining a critical engineer is a business necessity.
No increase is permitted off-cycle; retention must wait for the annual compensation cycle.
